plain_text:
TOWN OF HAMDEN, CONNECTICUT 
 
Tree Commission Minutes         
         
Regular Meeting 
 
5:30 PM, November 17, 2026 
 
 
 
Hamden Government 
Center 
2nd Floor Conference 
Room 
2750 Dixwell Avenue 
Hamden, CT  06518 
Tel:  (203) 287-7070 
Fax:  (203) 287-7075 
 Click to View Agenda   
  
1. CALL TO ORDER 
  
 The meeting was called to order by Chairman Commissioner Dr. M. Montgomery at 5:34 PM. 
2. ATTENDANCE 
  
 The Clerk called the roll, and the following members: 
Present  
Commissioner Dr. Michael Montgomery, Chair 
Commissioner Susan L. Neitlich 
Commissioner Diane E. Hoffman 
Commissioner Dr. Nathan Havill 
Commissioner Kyle Dougherty 
 
Also in attendance: Briana J. Belton-Robinson, Boards and Commissions Clerk, Andrew 
Kinlock, GIS Coordinator, and one resident joining virtually. 
 
Roll Call Summary: Present, Voting: 5; Present, Not Voting: 0; Absent: 0; Excused: 0. 
3. APPROVAL OF PREVIOUS MEETING MINUTES 
  
 
 
  1. Regular Meeting of October 20, 2026  
  The Commission reviewed the minutes of the October 20th, 2026 Regular Meeting. 
 
Chairman Dr. Montgomery moved to adopt the minutes from October 20th, 2026, with 
amendments.  
 
The following corrections were identified: 
• Under the "Old Business, Fall Planting" Section,  
1. Change "63 Barret Street" to "63 Burke Street" 
2. Change "47 Homeland Street" to "47 Homeland Terrace" 
3. Change "North Lane" to "North Street"
4. Change "....Darius Boyce's residence." to "...Trina Boyce's residence, 
mother of Darius Boyce." 
 
Commissioner D.E. Hoffman moved to approve the minutes, and Commissioner S.L. 
Neitlich seconded. 
 
The motion passed. 
4. PUBLIC COMMENT 
  
 No public comments were given. 
5. CORRESPONDENCE 
There will be a brief summary of the correspondence submitted between the last 
correspondence update and this one. This includes but is not limited to any 
correspondence with council members that members wish to submit for the record. It can 
also include written communication to the council from the administration, community 
members, etc.   
 Chairman Dr. M. Montgomery and Clerk B. Belton-Robinson checked the Commission 
email, and the following correspondence was received from Anjali Khanna, Urban Forest 
Network Coordinator for The Nature Conservancy, on Monday, November 16th, 2026: 
 
"Hi Hamden Tree Commission,  
 
Over the spring and fall, the Connecticut Urban Forest Network brought together 
practitioners from across the state through a series of Urban and Community Forestry Peer 
Learning Exchanges. Thank you to everyone who participated and shared their 
experiences, ideas, and expertise. To continue building connections and supporting peer 
learning, we are launching a series of Community of Practice calls. These conversations 
will create ongoing opportunities to connect with others across Connecticut who are 
working to improve community health, resilience, and quality of life through urban and 
community forestry.  
 
Join us for the Urban and Community Forestry Community of Practice call on November 
30th from 10:00-11:00! Hosted every three months, these calls are a great opportunity to 
connect with urban forestry practitioners from across the state to:  
 
Discuss common urban forestry challenges and brainstorm solutions  
Workshop projects  
Learn from the experiences and expertise of others in the field  
Build this urban forest network together  
 
Click here to register!   
 
Don’t miss out on this unique experience to learn from the many people (whether nonprofit 
professionals or municipal employees) leading this work around the state!  
 
What to expect: On the first call, we want to hear from you!
• What urban forestry topics are you most interested in discussing?  
• Do you have a project that you would like the opportunity to workshop with peers? 
• What would make these calls most supportive of your work?  
   
Also in attendance will be Grants Specialist Abbie Passero to share her expertise as it 
pertains to accessing and managing funding.  
 
Community of Practice calls grew out of the Urban and Community Forestry Peer Learning 
Exchanges, a series of half-day events where urban forestry practitioners within a council 
of governments region come together to learn from their neighboring municipalities, build 
connections for future collaborations, hear from statewide groups who provide technical 
and funding support, and workshop common urban forestry challenges. Community of 
Practice calls are an opportunity to keep these collaborative conversations moving forward! 
 
Thank you, 
 
Anjali Khanna" 
 
Chairman Dr. M. Montgomery requested that the Clerk forward the correspondence to all 
commissioners. The Clerk agreed. 
6. EXECUTIVE SESSION 
(if recommended by the town attorney)  
 No Executive Session was held. 
7. REPORTS 
  
 
 
  1. Tree Warden Report (e.g., Removals, Postings, Permits) 
• On-Call Arborist RFP 
  
  Tree Warden Report (e.g., Removals, Postings, Permits) 
 
Chairman Dr. M. Montgomery reported that he had spoken with the Tree Warden 
before the meeting. However, a formal written report regarding tree removals, 
postings, and permits was not available at the time of the meeting. 
Chairman Dr. M. Montgomery stated that tree-related activity appeared to be limited 
because Department of Public Works personnel were primarily occupied with 
seasonal leaf and brush collection. 
 
On-Call Arborist Request for Proposals (RFP) 
 
Chairman Dr. M. Montgomery reported that the Town received one application in 
response to the On-Call Arborist RFP from Eocene Environmental Group, a national 
environmental consulting company headquartered in Des Moines, Iowa, with 
operations in Connecticut.
The proposed arborist is based in Milford and possesses qualifications that Chairman 
Dr. M. Montgomery considered appropriate for the position. 
 
Chairman Dr. M. Montgomery reported that the proposed hourly rate appeared 
reasonable; however, the applicant requested a minimum commitment of 16 hours per 
week. 
 
The Town's Purchasing Department continues to review the application. No final 
determination regarding the contract has been made. 
Chairman Dr. M. Montgomery stated that he had previously researched approximately 
ten arborists within a 25-mile radius of Hamden to identify individuals who might 
possess the qualifications outlined in the RFP. Of those identified, approximately two 
appeared particularly well qualified. 
 
He noted that the Commission could help identify potential applicants if the Town 
needs to issue another RFP. 
 
Swarthmore Street Tree Evaluations 
 
Commissioners requested an update regarding the evaluation of trees along 
Swarthmore Street. 
Chairman Dr. M. Montgomery stated that the need for professional tree evaluations 
was one reason the Town was pursuing an on-call consulting arborist. No additional 
update was available. 
8. OLD BUSINESS 
  
 
 
  1. Trees for Communities Grant  
  CT DEEP Grant Reporting Requirements 
 
Chairman Dr. M. Montgomery reported that he and Commissioner S.L. Neitlich 
attended the monthly grant meeting with the Connecticut Department of Energy and 
Environmental Protection (CT DEEP), during which additional reporting requirements 
were discussed. 
Through the Urban Forest Resilience Grant Program, CT DEEP requested geographic 
coordinates for trees planted under the grant, with an initial submission deadline of 
November 16, 2026. 
 
Chairman Dr. M. Montgomery explained that the Commission's 
approximately $120,000 grant supports the planting of 120 trees. Approximately 50 
trees had been planted to date, including nine during the spring planting season and 
approximately 44 during the fall planting season. 
 
CT DEEP requested approximate geographic coordinates to facilitate site visits and 
evaluate the Commission's planting practices. A comprehensive record containing the 
geographic coordinates of all trees planted under the grant will ultimately be required 
for final reporting.
Commissioner S.L. Neitlich reported that she had photographed the identification tags 
of trees on which trunk protectors had been installed. The photographs contain 
geographic location information that can be extracted and incorporated into the 
Commission's grant reporting spreadsheet. 
 
Chairman Dr. M. Montgomery demonstrated how geographic coordinates could be 
retrieved from photographs using a mobile device. He explained that photographing 
the identification tags also provides an opportunity to verify the species and cultivars 
planted at each location against the Commission's purchasing and planting records. 
 
Commissioner K. Dougherty emphasized the importance of ensuring that the 
geographic coordinates are recorded in a consistent and accurate format. He noted 
that longitude coordinates expressed in decimal degrees must include the appropriate 
negative sign to indicate locations west of the prime meridian. Alternatively, the 
appropriate north and west directional indicators must be included. 
 
Commissioner K. Dougherty offered to assist with reviewing and correcting the 
coordinate formatting before submission. 
 
Commissioner S.L. Neitlich asked whether photographs and geographic coordinates 
should also be collected for trees that had not yet received trunk protectors. 
 
Chairman Dr. M. Montgomery stated that the Commission should ultimately obtain 
photographs and coordinates for every tree. However, because CT DEEP was initially 
requesting a sampling of planting locations, the Commission could submit the 
information currently available and complete the remaining entries afterward. 
 
Chairman Dr. M. Montgomery acknowledged that the initial submission would be 
slightly delayed. 
 
Grant Purchases and Educational Materials 
 
The Commission discussed outstanding purchases associated with the Trees for 
Communities Grant, including: 
 
• Educational door hangers for residents receiving trees. 
• Educational books. 
• Labeling materials for tree-watering bags. 
• Graphic materials incorporating the Hamden Tree Commission's logo. 
 
Chairman Dr. M. Montgomery expressed a preference for consolidating purchases 
into a single purchase order whenever possible because of the administrative 
workload associated with the Town's purchasing and grant reimbursement processes. 
 
He explained that each purchase requires substantial documentation, processing, and 
financial reconciliation by Town staff. 
 
Following discussion, the Commission agreed to proceed with the purchase of the
educational books and temporarily postpone the purchase of the door hangers and 
other graphic and labeling materials until the remaining designs and purchasing 
requirements were finalized. 
 
Chairman Dr. M. Montgomery stated that he would submit the purchase order for the 
books. 
 
Fall Tree Planting Update 
 
Commissioner K. Dougherty asked Chairman Dr. M. Montgomery whether the 
remaining trees scheduled for fall planting had been planted. 
 
Chairman Dr. M. Montgomery provided an update on the remaining trees and 
discussed several logistical challenges encountered during the fall planting season, 
including contractor availability, tree transportation, planting locations, and the 
physical demands associated with planting larger trees. 
 
The Commission discussed contractor-assisted planting at ConnCORP, where seven 
trees were planted, and considered the financial implications of relying on contractors 
for future planting activities. 
 
Chairman Dr. M. Montgomery expressed a preference for utilizing volunteers 
whenever practical, particularly when planting trees on private residential properties. 
 
He stated that volunteer participation provides opportunities for community 
engagement, strengthens relationships with residents, and encourages residents to 
take an active role in the planting and long-term stewardship of their trees. 
 
The Commission acknowledged that professional contractors may still be necessary 
for larger trees, challenging planting locations, or projects requiring specialized 
equipment. 
 
Future Tree Procurement and Planting Procedures 
 
Chairman Dr. M. Montgomery discussed potential improvements to the Commission's 
tree procurement process for the 2027 planting season. 
 
He proposed exploring the advance purchase of bare-root trees from suppliers on the 
West Coast and nurseries in western New York. 
Under the proposed approach, trees could be received in advance, transferred into 
growing containers, and maintained for approximately three months before being 
planted at their permanent locations. 
 
Chairman Dr. M. Montgomery explained that this approach could provide several 
advantages, including: 
 
• Improved access to a wider selection of tree species and cultivars. 
• Reduced transportation and shipping costs. 
• Greater flexibility in coordinating planting activities.
• Reduced dependence on contractors and heavy equipment. 
• Improved opportunities for volunteer-assisted planting. 
• Easier handling of container-grown trees compared with heavier balled-and-
burlapped trees. 
 
Chairman Dr. M. Montgomery discussed ordering approximately 20–30 trees in 
advance and identifying suitable planting locations based on available inventory. 
 
The Commission discussed establishing a more limited catalog of available trees for 
residents. Commissioners would present residents with selections of the species and 
cultivars the Commission intended to procure rather than offer an unrestricted 
selection of trees. 
 
Commissioner S.L. Neitlich shared examples of the tree selections offered through 
Hartford's tree-planting program, which categorizes available trees by mature size. 
 
The Commission discussed using a similar approach to help residents select 
appropriate trees based on available space, site conditions, and anticipated mature 
tree size. 
 
Volunteer Recruitment and Student Engagement 
 
The Commission discussed opportunities to expand volunteer participation in future 
tree planting activities. 
 
Chairman Dr. M. Montgomery identified the environmental club at Hamden High 
School as a potential partner. Commissioners discussed engaging students in 
planting activities and exploring opportunities for compensated participation where 
appropriate. 
 
The Commission also discussed the importance of providing volunteers with 
appropriate training and ensuring planting assignments suit participants' experience 
and physical capabilities. 
 
Commissioner S.L. Neitlich reported that the Commission had completed nearly all 
activities documented in its shared 2026 activity and volunteer tracking spreadsheet, 
with the upcoming Hamden High School environmental club engagement remaining 
on the schedule. 
 
Commissioner S.L. Neitlich stated that she would prepare a new shared document for 
2027 to continue tracking Commission activities, volunteer participation, and service 
hours. 
  2. Tree Inventory  
  At the request of Chairman Dr. M. Montgomery, the Commission addressed the Tree 
Inventory agenda item earlier in the meeting to accommodate the attendance of GIS 
Coordinator A. Kinlock. 
 
Existing Geographic Information System (GIS) Infrastructure
Chairman Dr. M. Montgomery welcomed Coordinator A. Kinlock to discuss the Town's 
existing GIS infrastructure and opportunities to develop a comprehensive municipal 
tree inventory. 
 
Chairman Dr. M. Montgomery reported that he had reviewed portions of the Town's 
existing tree inventory and discovered that a section of Swarthmore Street had 
previously been surveyed. 
 
He noted that some of the information appeared outdated, including records for trees 
that had subsequently been removed and diameter-at-breast-height (DBH) 
measurements that no longer reflected the current size of existing trees. 
 
Coordinator A. Kinlock explained that the inventory was developed several years 
earlier as part of an initiative to determine whether students participating in the Town's 
summer youth employment program could assist with GIS mapping. 
 
Coordinator A. Kinlock stated that the project had subsequently been placed on hold 
when the Engineering Department shifted its priorities toward sidewalk mapping and 
infrastructure assessments. 
 
With portions of the sidewalk mapping initiative now completed, opportunities may 
exist to resume tree inventory activities. 
 
CT DEEP Tree Inventory Software and Grant Opportunities 
 
Chairman Dr. M. Montgomery reported that CT DEEP was exploring the acquisition of 
a software platform that could be made available to municipalities through 
sublicensing arrangements. 
 
He explained that a state-supported platform could provide municipalities with 
technical assistance and potentially improve access for Commission members and 
volunteers who do not have Town-issued GIS accounts. 
 
Chairman Dr. M. Montgomery proposed coordinating a meeting with Coordinator A. 
Kinlock and a representative from CT DEEP's Urban Forestry Program to compare 
the Town's existing GIS infrastructure with the proposed state-supported platform. 
 
The meeting would help determine which platform would be most appropriate for 
developing, maintaining, and updating Hamden's tree inventory. 
 
Chairman Dr. M. Montgomery also discussed the availability of CT DEEP grants 
supporting municipal tree inventories. 
 
He emphasized that a comprehensive tree inventory is a foundational component of 
an effective municipal urban forestry management program. 
 
Grant funding could potentially support personnel responsible for collecting inventory 
data, while Commission members could provide training in tree identification, 
measurement, and data collection.
Youth Employment and Professional Development 
 
Coordinator A. Kinlock recommended including students in the Town's summer youth 
employment program in the tree inventory initiative. 
He explained that the program provides Hamden young with opportunities to develop: 
 
• Geographic information system and data collection skills. 
• Professional and technical experience. 
• Teamwork and communication skills. 
• Workplace readiness. 
• Opportunities for future employment and career exploration. 
 
Coordinator A. Kinlock reported that he had worked with approximately five to six 
student interns during six-week summer sessions over several years. 
 
He emphasized the importance of preserving opportunities for students to participate 
in meaningful municipal projects that contribute to their professional development. 
 
Commissioner K. Dougherty stated that the Commission's primary objective was to 
establish a comprehensive tree inventory because the lack of accessible baseline 
information limits its ability to evaluate and manage Hamden's urban forest. 
 
Coordinator A. Kinlock agreed that establishing baseline information was necessary to 
measure changes in tree canopy and support future urban forestry planning. 
 
Commissioner Participation and Next Steps 
 
Commissioner S.L. Neitlich expressed interest in having all commissioners participate 
in an educational session regarding the GIS platform and tree inventory procedures. 
 
She noted that all commissioners had previously expressed a willingness to assist 
with inventory activities. 
 
Coordinator A. Kinlock recommended that an initial meeting occur to evaluate the 
available GIS platforms before determining how information would be collected, 
maintained, and shared with commissioners and other participants. 
 
Chairman Dr. M. Montgomery agreed to coordinate the preliminary meeting and 
provide Coordinator A. Kinlock with an electronic copy of the Commission's current 
tree planting and geographic coordinate spreadsheet. 
 
The Commission thanked Coordinator A. Kinlock for attending the meeting. 
  3. Activities with Hamden Public Library  
  Commissioner K. Dougherty reported that the tree map associated with the 
Commission's educational activities at the Hamden Public Library requires updating.
Commissioner K. Dougherty stated that he intends to work on updating the map 
during the winter months. 
 
The Commission also discussed opportunities to expand public awareness and 
appreciation of Hamden's notable trees through educational materials, mapping, and 
public outreach. 
 
Notable Trees Initiative 
 
Commissioner K. Dougherty expressed interest in expanding the Commission's work 
on notable trees following his recent educational presentation. 
 
He stated that he intends to measure several trees throughout Hamden during the 
winter and requested that commissioners consider how the information could be used 
to increase public awareness and appreciation of the Town's urban forest. 
 
Potential opportunities discussed included incorporating the information into the 
municipal tree inventory, publishing educational information on the Commission's 
webpage, and preparing educational features for the Town's social media platforms. 
 
Chairman Dr. M. Montgomery requested that Commissioner K. Dougherty measure 
one of the larger pin oak trees on Swarthmore Street and report at the next meeting 
how its size compares with other notable pin oak trees in Hamden and throughout 
Connecticut. 
 
 
Additional Tree Planting and Stewardship Discussion 
 
Residential Landscaping and Community Engagement 
 
Commissioner S.L. Neitlich reported on residential landscaping activities involving Jan 
and her husband, Danny. The planting included two Little Henry sweetspire (Itea) 
shrubs and two clumps of bearberry. 
 
The Commission discussed the value of incorporating complementary vegetation into 
residential planting projects and engaging residents in the stewardship of newly 
planted trees. 
 
Contracted Tree Planting Costs 
 
Chairman Dr. M. Montgomery reported that the anticipated cost associated with 
planting seven trees at ConnCORP was less than $2,500. 
 
He reiterated his preference for volunteer-assisted planting whenever feasible to 
maximize available grant resources and encourage community participation. 
 
Memorial Tree Plantings 
 
Chairman Dr. M. Montgomery discussed requests for memorial tree plantings and the 
potential establishment of a designated memorial grove where residents could
commemorate loved ones through tree donations. 
 
He identified Eli Whitney Park near Davis Street as a potential location for further 
consideration. 
 
The Commission discussed the potential use of existing tree trust funds or donation 
funds to support memorial plantings that are not eligible for reimbursement under the 
CT DEEP grant. 
 
No formal action was taken regarding the establishment of a memorial grove. 
 
Repurposing Wood from Removed Trees 
 
Commissioner S.L. Neitlich reported that, during the CT DEEP monthly grant meeting, 
another grant recipient discussed an initiative in Hartford that repurposes wood from 
removed trees into furniture and other wood products. 
 
Commissioner S.L. Neitlich inquired whether wood from trees removed in Hamden 
could be donated to the organization. She was informed that this would be possible, 
provided appropriate transportation could be arranged. 
 
The Commission discussed the potential environmental and economic benefits of 
repurposing removed trees rather than disposing of or chipping usable hardwood. 
 
Chairman Dr. M. Montgomery noted that similar initiatives exist in Connecticut and 
that wood from previously removed trees has been repurposed for municipal use. 
 
Commissioner K. Dougherty also shared that he had previously collected oak logs 
from removed trees in Hamden for mushroom cultivation. 
9. NEW BUSINESS 
  
 2026 Commission Activities and Volunteer Hours 
 
Commissioner S.L. Neitlich reported that all activities identified in the shared Google 
document she previously distributed to commissioners, which tracks Commission activities, 
volunteer participation, and volunteer hours, had been completed, with the exception of the 
upcoming engagement with the ECO Club at Hamden High School. 
 
Two Tree Commissioners and one representative from the Hamden Alliance for Trees 
(HAT) are expected to participate in the remaining activity. 
 
Commissioner S.L. Neitlich stated that she would prepare a new shared Google document 
for 2027 to continue tracking Commission activities and volunteer hours. 
 
South Central Regional Council of Governments (SCRCOG) Survey 
 
Commissioner D.E. Hoffman inquired whether the Town of Hamden had participated in a 
survey conducted by the South Central Regional Council of Governments (SCRCOG).
Chairman Dr. M. Montgomery confirmed that Hamden had participated in the survey. He 
explained that there may have been some confusion regarding the survey because of a 
separate suitability project in which the Town was already engaged. 
 
Chairman Dr. M. Montgomery also stated that he would distribute the survey conducted by 
Yale University students, which includes a map of Hamden and information pertaining to 
zoning regulations and municipal ordinances. 
 
Sustainable CT Certification 
 
Chairman Dr. M. Montgomery discussed the Town's participation in Sustainable CT and 
the Commission's contributions to municipal sustainability initiatives, including tree planting, 
tree stewardship, municipal tree ordinances, and opportunities for residents to contribute 
financially toward tree planting. 
 
Chairman Dr. M. Montgomery reported that Hamden had received the highest level of 
recognition awarded through the Sustainable CT certification program. 
 
Arbor Day Foundation — Tree City USA 
 
Chairman Dr. M. Montgomery reported that the Town of Hamden is required to submit an 
annual report to the Arbor Day Foundation to maintain its Tree City USA designation. 
 
The annual reporting requirements include information regarding municipal tree-related 
expenditures, urban forestry activities, and tree management practices. 
 
Chairman Dr. M. Montgomery noted that the annual report submitted by the Town is not 
routinely shared with the Tree Commission. 
  1. Meeting Agenda Procedures  
  Meeting Agenda Procedures 
 
Chairman Dr. M. Montgomery reviewed correspondence from Town Clerk K. Mickens 
regarding updated procedures for the submission and posting of meeting agendas for 
municipal boards and commissions. 
 
Effective immediately, boards and commissions are requested to submit their meeting 
agendas to their assigned Boards and Commissions Clerk at least three business 
days before the required public posting deadline. 
 
Chairman Dr. M. Montgomery explained that the updated procedures are intended to 
ensure sufficient time for administrative review, preparation, distribution, and posting 
of meeting notices. 
 
The Commission discussed its existing procedures for developing meeting agendas. 
Chairman Dr. M. Montgomery stated that he generally requests proposed agenda 
items from commissioners by Wednesday evening preceding the regular meeting. 
 
The Commission also discussed the importance of allowing sufficient time for 
commissioners to review proposed agenda items and submit any additional matters
for consideration. 
 
Chairman Dr. M. Montgomery noted that meeting agendas must also be submitted to 
the Town Clerk's Office, with Town Clerk K. Mickens copied on the correspondence. 
 
Chairman Dr. M. Montgomery emphasized that meeting notices must be posted 
electronically and physically on the Town Clerk's designated bulletin board in 
accordance with applicable public meeting requirements. 
 
The Clerk confirmed that meeting agendas are distributed to the appropriate municipal 
personnel as part of the existing posting process. 
 
Chairman Dr. M. Montgomery stated that the Commission would continue working to 
ensure compliance with the updated agenda submission procedures. 
 
 
Freedom of Information (FOI) Requirements and Educational Activities 
 
The Commission discussed Connecticut Freedom of Information requirements as they 
relate to commissioners participating in educational activities, volunteer projects, 
community events, and informational sessions outside regularly scheduled 
Commission meetings. 
 
Commissioner D.E. Hoffman requested clarification regarding whether multiple 
commissioners, including a quorum of the Commission, could attend educational 
activities together when the purpose of the gathering is to acquire knowledge rather 
than deliberate or conduct Commission business. 
 
Commissioners expressed interest in ensuring that all members have opportunities to 
participate in professional development and educational activities relevant to their 
responsibilities. 
 
The proposed meeting with GIS Coordinator A. Kinlock and a representative from CT 
DEEP was identified as an example of an informational gathering for which 
clarification would be beneficial. 
 
The Commission discussed whether such a gathering would require a formally noticed 
special meeting or whether commissioners could participate solely for educational 
purposes. 
 
Chairman Dr. M. Montgomery acknowledged that the proposed GIS discussion relates 
to Commission business, although its initial purpose would be to obtain technical 
information regarding available tree inventory platforms. 
 
The Clerk recommended obtaining further clarification regarding applicable FOI 
requirements. 
 
Chairman Dr. M. Montgomery reported that he was scheduled to meet virtually with 
Town Clerk K. Mickens on Thursday, November 19, 2026, to discuss meeting 
procedures and related administrative matters.
He agreed to raise the Commission's questions regarding: 
 
• Commissioner participation in educational and professional development 
activities. 
• Attendance by a quorum of commissioners at informational sessions. 
• Volunteer activities and community engagement events. 
• The distinction between educational gatherings and meetings involving 
Commission business. 
• Public notice requirements for gatherings involving multiple commissioners. 
 
Chairman Dr. M. Montgomery stated that Town Clerk K. Mickens could refer questions 
requiring further interpretation to the appropriate state Freedom of Information 
officials. 
 
No formal determination regarding the applicability of FOI requirements to the 
proposed educational sessions was made during the meeting. 
 
 
Sustainable CT and Tree City USA 
 
Chairman Dr. M. Montgomery discussed Hamden's participation in Sustainable CT 
and recent inquiries regarding municipal sustainability initiatives. 
 
The discussion included the Town's tree ordinance, tree planting and stewardship 
activities, and opportunities for residents to make financial contributions toward 
municipal tree planting. 
 
Chairman Dr. M. Montgomery clarified that the Town's mechanism for accepting 
donations toward tree planting and other environmental initiatives was established by 
the Legislative Council. 
 
He also reported that he had previously assisted Town personnel with providing 
information regarding the Commission's activities in support of Hamden's Sustainable 
CT certification efforts. 
 
Chairman Dr. M. Montgomery noted that Hamden had achieved an advanced level of 
sustainability recognition. 
 
The Commission also discussed Hamden's Tree City USA designation through the 
Arbor Day Foundation. 
 
Chairman Dr. M. Montgomery explained that maintaining the designation requires the 
Town to submit annual information regarding municipal tree-related expenditures, 
activities, and urban forestry practices. 
 
He noted that the annual report submitted by the Town is not routinely shared with the 
Tree Commission.
2027 Commission Activity and Volunteer Tracking 
 
Commissioner S.L. Neitlich reported that the Commission had completed the activities 
identified in its shared 2026 tracking document, with the exception of the upcoming 
engagement with the environmental club at Hamden High School. 
 
Commissioner S.L. Neitlich stated that she would develop a new shared Google 
document for 2027 to continue documenting: 
 
• Commission activities and community events. 
• Volunteer participation. 
• Commissioner participation. 
• Volunteer and service hours. 
• Educational and outreach initiatives. 
 
The document will assist the Commission with maintaining accurate records of its 
annual activities and supporting future reporting requirements. 
10. ADJOURNMENT 
  
 There being no further business, Chairman Dr. M. Montgomery asked whether there were any 
objections to adjournment. 
 
Hearing none, the meeting was adjourned at 7:21 pm
